title: Two ways a bond can break
caption: In homolytic fission each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair, giving two radicals (half-headed arrows). In heterolytic fission the more electronegative atom takes both electrons, giving a cation and an anion (a full curly arrow).
alt: Two rows: C–Br breaking homolytically into CH₃• and Br•, and heterolytically into CH₃⁺ and Br⁻.
description: Homolytic: CH₃–Br → CH₃• + Br•, one electron each.
Heterolytic: CH₃–Br → CH₃⁺ + Br⁻, bromine takes both.
